patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — VTEX and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

VTEX and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose VTEX only if your buying job matches “Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. Shopify kee” rather than WooCommerce's shape. Choose WooCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPaymen” rather than VTEX's shape. Workflow advantage: VTEX leans wholesale-b2b; WooCommerce leans catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — VTEX and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: VTEX is Enterprise commerce SaaS — contact-sales get-started only; no invented floors. Shopify keeps the SaaS award.; WooCommerce is Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPayments processing are separate TCO lines..
- Company-size focus: VTEX (mid-market, enterprise) vs WooCommerce (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: VTEX-leaning wholesale-b2b vs WooCommerce-leaning catalog-management.
- Researched limits: VTEX — No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone; WooCommerce — You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS.

Limitations — VTEX: No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone; Enterprise sales and implementation cycles versus Shopify SMB speed; WooCommerce: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS; Extension sprawl can inflate TCO and maintenance.

Poor-fit cases: VTEX is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No published self-serve monthly tiles — hard to shortlist on list price alone · WooCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS · Avoid VTEX if you actually need WooCommerce's motion (Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
